00004| description: Learn how to cache and revalidate data using fetch options, unstable_cache, and route segment configs for projects not using Cache Components.
00005| ---
00006| 
00007| > This guide assumes you are **not** using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) which was introduced in version 16 under the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents).
00008| 
00009| ## Caching `fetch` requests
00010| 
00011| By default, [`fetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) requests are not cached. You can cache individual requests by setting the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`.
00012| 
00013| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00014| export default async function Page() {
00015|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
00016| }
00017| ```
00018| 
00019| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00020| export default async function Page() {
00021|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { cache: 'force-cache' })
00022| }
00023| ```
00024| 
00025| See the [`fetch` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch) to learn more.
00026| 
00027| ### `unstable_cache` for non-`fetch` functions
00028| 
00029| `unstable_cache` allows you to cache the result of database queries and other async functions that don't use `fetch`. Wrap `unstable_cache` around the function:
00030| 
00031| ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00032| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00033| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00034| 
00035| export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00036|   async (id: string) => {
00037|     return db
00038|       .select()
00039|       .from(users)
00040|       .where(eq(users.id, id))
00041|       .then((res) => res[0])
00042|   },
00043|   ['user'], // cache key prefix
00044|   {
00045|     tags: ['user'],
00046|     revalidate: 3600,
00047|   }
00048| )
00049| ```
00050| 
00051| ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00052| import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'
00053| import { db } from '@/lib/db'
00054| 
00055| export const getCachedUser = unstable_cache(
00056|   async (id) => {
00057|     return db
00058|       .select()
00059|       .from(users)
00060|       .where(eq(users.id, id))
00061|       .then((res) => res[0])
00062|   },
00063|   ['user'], // cache key prefix
00064|   {
00065|     tags: ['user'],
00066|     revalidate: 3600,
00067|   }
00068| )
00069| ```
00070| 
00071| The third argument accepts:
00072| 
00073| - `tags`: an array of tags for on-demand revalidation with `revalidateTag`.
00074| - `revalidate`: the number of seconds before the cache is revalidated.
00075| 
00076| See the [`unstable_cache` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) to learn more.
00077| 
00078| ### Route segment config
00079| 
00080| You can configure caching behavior at the route level by exporting config options from a [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00081| 
00082| #### `dynamic`
00083| 
00084| Change the dynamic behavior of a layout or page to fully static or fully dynamic.
00085| 
00086| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00087| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00088| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00089| ```
00090| 
00091| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00092| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00093| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
00097| - **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
00098|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
00099|   - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
00100| - **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
00101|   - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
00102|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
00103|   - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
00104| - **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
00105| 
00106| #### `fetchCache`
00107| 
00108| <details>
00109|   <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
00110| 
00111| A `fetch` request that sets no `cache` option is fetched once during `next build` if it is reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used, because the route is prerendered up to that point. Requests discovered **after** a Request-time API run on every request.
00112| 
00113| `fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00116| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00117| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00118| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00119| ```
00120| 
00121| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00122| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00123| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00124| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00125| ```
00126| 
00127| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
00128| - **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
00129| - **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
00130| - **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
00131| - **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
00132| - **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`
00133| - **`'force-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'no-store'`. This forces all `fetch` requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a `'force-cache'` option.
00134| 
00135| ##### Cross-route segment behavior
00136| 
00137| - Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
00138|   - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. The force option changes the behavior across the route so a single segment with `'force-*'` would prevent any errors caused by `'only-*'`.
00139|   - The intention of the `'only-*'` and `'force-*'` options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means:
00140|     - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00141|     - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00142|   - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.
00143| - It is generally recommended to leave shared parent layouts as `'auto'` and customize the options where child segments diverge.
00144| 
00145| </details>
00146| 
00147| ## Time-based revalidation
00148| 
00149| Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
00150| 
00151| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00152| export default async function Page() {
00153|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00158| export default async function Page() {
00159|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00160| }
00161| ```
00162| 
00163| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00164| 
00165| ### Route segment config `revalidate`
00166| 
00167| Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00170| export const revalidate = false
00171| // false | 0 | number
00172| ```
00173| 
00174| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00175| export const revalidate = false
00176| // false | 0 | number
00177| ```
00178| 
00179| - **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
00180| - **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of `fetch` requests that do not set a `cache` option to `'no-store'` but leaves `fetch` requests that opt into `'force-cache'` or use a positive `revalidate` as is.
00181| - **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
00182| 
00183| > **Good to know**:
00184| >
00185| > - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
00186| > - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
00187| > - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
00188| 
00189| #### Revalidation frequency
00190| 
00191| - The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
00192| - Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
00193| 
00194| ## On-demand revalidation
00195| 
00196| To revalidate cached data after an event, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00197| 
00198| ### Tagging cached data
00199| 
00200| Tag `fetch` requests with `next.tags` to enable on-demand cache invalidation:
00201| 
00202| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00203| export async function getUserById(id: string) {
00204|   const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
00205|     next: { tags: ['user'] },
00206|   })
00207| }
00208| ```
00209| 
00210| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00211| export async function getUserById(id) {
00212|   const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
00213|     next: { tags: ['user'] },
00214|   })
00215| }
00216| ```
00217| 
00218| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` also accepts a `tags` option (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00219| 
00220| ### `revalidateTag`
00221| 
00222| Invalidate cached data by tag using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag):
00223| 
00224| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
00225| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00226| 
00227| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00228|   // Mutate data
00229|   revalidateTag('user', 'max')
00230| }
00231| ```
00232| 
00233| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
00234| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00235| 
00236| export async function updateUser(id) {
00237|   // Mutate data
00238|   revalidateTag('user', 'max')
00239| }
00240| ```
00241| 
00242| ### `revalidatePath`
00243| 
00244| Invalidate all cached data for a specific route path using [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath):
00245| 
00246| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
00247| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00248| 
00249| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00250|   // Mutate data
00251|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00252| }
00253| ```
00254| 
00255| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
00256| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00257| 
00258| export async function updateUser(id) {
00259|   // Mutate data
00260|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00261| }
00262| ```
00263| 
00264| ## Deduplicating requests
00265| 
00266| If you are not using `fetch` (which is [automatically memoized](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization)), and instead using an ORM or database directly, you can wrap your data access with the [React `cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) function to deduplicate requests within a single render pass:
00267| 
00268| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00269| import { cache } from 'react'
00270| import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
00271| 
00272| export const getPost = cache(async (id: string) => {
00273|   const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
00274|     where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
00275|   })
00276| })
00277| ```
00278| 
00279| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00280| import { cache } from 'react'
00281| import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
00282| 
00283| export const getPost = cache(async (id) => {
00284|   const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
00285|     where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
00286|   })
00287| })
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| ## Preloading data
00291| 
00292| You can preload data by creating a utility function that you eagerly call above blocking requests. This lets you initiate data fetching early, so the data is already available by the time the component renders.
00293| 
00294| Combine the [`server-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) with React's [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to create a reusable preload utility:
00295| 
00296| ```ts filename="utils/get-item.ts" switcher
00297| import { cache } from 'react'
00298| import 'server-only'
00299| 
00300| export const getItem = cache(async (id: string) => {
00301|   // ...
00302| })
00303| 
00304| export const preload = (id: string) => {
00305|   void getItem(id)
00306| }
00307| ```
00308| 
00309| ```js filename="utils/get-item.js" switcher
00310| import { cache } from 'react'
00311| import 'server-only'
00312| 
00313| export const getItem = cache(async (id) => {
00314|   // ...
00315| })
00316| 
00317| export const preload = (id) => {
00318|   void getItem(id)
00319| }
00320| ```
00321| 
00322| Then call `preload()` before any blocking work so the data starts loading immediately:
00323| 
00324| ```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
00325| import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
00326| 
00327| export default async function Page({
00328|   params,
00329| }: {
00330|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00331| }) {
00332|   const { id } = await params
00333|   // Start loading item data
00334|   preload(id)
00335|   // Perform another asynchronous task
00336|   const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()
00337| 
00338|   return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
00339| }
00340| 
00341| async function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
00342|   const result = await getItem(id)
00343|   // ...
00344| }
00345| ```

00092| export const dynamic = 'auto'
00093| // 'auto' | 'force-dynamic' | 'error' | 'force-static'
00094| ```
00095| 
00096| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache as much as possible without preventing any components from opting into dynamic behavior.
00097| - **`'force-dynamic'`**: Force [dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering), which will result in routes being rendered for each user at request time. This option is equivalent to:
00098|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'no-store', next: { revalidate: 0 } }`.
00099|   - Setting the segment config to `export const fetchCache = 'force-no-store'`
00100| - **`'error'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by causing an error if any components use Request-time APIs or uncached data. This option is equivalent to:
00101|   - `getStaticProps()` in the `pages` directory.
00102|   - Setting the option of every `fetch()` request in a layout or page to `{ cache: 'force-cache' }`.
00103|   - Setting the segment config to `fetchCache = 'only-cache'`.
00104| - **`'force-static'`**: Force prerendering and cache the data of a layout or page by forcing [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) to return empty values. It is possible to [`revalidate`](#route-segment-config-revalidate), [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag), in pages or layouts rendered with `force-static`.
00105| 
00106| #### `fetchCache`
00107| 
00108| <details>
00109|   <summary>This is an advanced option that should only be used if you specifically need to override the default behavior.</summary>
00110| 
00111| A `fetch` request that sets no `cache` option is fetched once during `next build` if it is reachable **before** any Request-time APIs are used, because the route is prerendered up to that point. Requests discovered **after** a Request-time API run on every request.
00112| 
00113| `fetchCache` allows you to override the default `cache` option of all `fetch` requests in a layout or page.
00114| 
00115| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00116| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00117| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00118| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00119| ```
00120| 
00121| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00122| export const fetchCache = 'auto'
00123| // 'auto' | 'default-cache' | 'only-cache'
00124| // 'force-cache' | 'force-no-store' | 'default-no-store' | 'only-no-store'
00125| ```
00126| 
00127| - **`'auto'`** (default): The default option to cache `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs with the `cache` option they provide and not cache `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs.
00128| - **`'default-cache'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'force-cache'`. This means that even `fetch` requests after Request-time APIs are considered static.
00129| - **`'only-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by changing the default to `cache: 'force-cache'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'no-store'`.
00130| - **`'force-cache'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt into caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'force-cache'`.
00131| - **`'default-no-store'`**: Allow any `cache` option to be passed to `fetch` but if no option is provided then set the `cache` option to `'no-store'`. This means that even `fetch` requests before Request-time APIs are considered dynamic.
00132| - **`'only-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by changing the default to `cache: 'no-store'` if no option is provided and causing an error if any `fetch` requests use `cache: 'force-cache'`
00133| - **`'force-no-store'`**: Ensure all `fetch` requests opt out of caching by setting the `cache` option of all `fetch` requests to `'no-store'`. This forces all `fetch` requests to be re-fetched every request even if they provide a `'force-cache'` option.
00134| 
00135| ##### Cross-route segment behavior
00136| 
00137| - Any options set across each layout and page of a single route need to be compatible with each other.
00138|   - If both the `'only-cache'` and `'force-cache'` are provided, then `'force-cache'` wins. If both `'only-no-store'` and `'force-no-store'` are provided, then `'force-no-store'` wins. The force option changes the behavior across the route so a single segment with `'force-*'` would prevent any errors caused by `'only-*'`.
00139|   - The intention of the `'only-*'` and `'force-*'` options is to guarantee the whole route is either fully static or fully dynamic. This means:
00140|     - A combination of `'only-cache'` and `'only-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00141|     - A combination of `'force-cache'` and `'force-no-store'` in a single route is not allowed.
00142|   - A parent cannot provide `'default-no-store'` if a child provides `'auto'` or `'*-cache'` since that could make the same fetch have different behavior.
00143| - It is generally recommended to leave shared parent layouts as `'auto'` and customize the options where child segments diverge.
00144| 
00145| </details>
00146| 
00147| ## Time-based revalidation
00148| 
00149| Use the `next.revalidate` option on `fetch` to revalidate data after a specified number of seconds:
00150| 
00151| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00152| export default async function Page() {
00153|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher
00158| export default async function Page() {
00159|   const data = await fetch('https://...', { next: { revalidate: 3600 } })
00160| }
00161| ```
00162| 
00163| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` accepts a `revalidate` option in its configuration (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00164| 
00165| ### Route segment config `revalidate`
00166| 
00167| Set the default revalidation time for a layout or page. This option does not override the `revalidate` value set by individual `fetch` requests.
00168| 
00169| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx | route.ts" switcher
00170| export const revalidate = false
00171| // false | 0 | number
00172| ```
00173| 
00174| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js | route.js" switcher
00175| export const revalidate = false
00176| // false | 0 | number
00177| ```
00178| 
00179| - **`false`** (default): The default heuristic to cache any `fetch` requests that set their `cache` option to `'force-cache'` or are discovered before a Request-time API is used. Semantically equivalent to `revalidate: Infinity` which effectively means the resource should be cached indefinitely. It is still possible for individual `fetch` requests to use `cache: 'no-store'` or `revalidate: 0` to avoid being cached and make the route dynamically rendered. Or set `revalidate` to a positive number lower than the route default to increase the revalidation frequency of a route.
00180| - **`0`**: Ensure a layout or page is always dynamically rendered even if no Request-time APIs or uncached data fetches are discovered. This option changes the default of `fetch` requests that do not set a `cache` option to `'no-store'` but leaves `fetch` requests that opt into `'force-cache'` or use a positive `revalidate` as is.
00181| - **`number`**: (in seconds) Set the default revalidation frequency of a layout or page to `n` seconds.
00182| 
00183| > **Good to know**:
00184| >
00185| > - The revalidate value needs to be statically analyzable. For example `revalidate = 600` is valid, but `revalidate = 60 * 10` is not.
00186| > - The revalidate value is not available when using the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`.
00187| > - In Development, Pages are _always_ rendered on-demand and are never cached. This allows you to see changes immediately without waiting for a revalidation period to pass.
00188| 
00189| #### Revalidation frequency
00190| 
00191| - The lowest `revalidate` across each layout and page of a single route will determine the revalidation frequency of the _entire_ route. This ensures that child pages are revalidated as frequently as their parent layouts.
00192| - Individual `fetch` requests can set a lower `revalidate` than the route's default `revalidate` to increase the revalidation frequency of the entire route. This allows you to dynamically opt-in to more frequent revalidation for certain routes based on some criteria.
00193| 
00194| ## On-demand revalidation
00195| 
00196| To revalidate cached data after an event, use [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00197| 
00198| ### Tagging cached data
00199| 
00200| Tag `fetch` requests with `next.tags` to enable on-demand cache invalidation:
00201| 
00202| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00203| export async function getUserById(id: string) {
00204|   const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
00205|     next: { tags: ['user'] },
00206|   })
00207| }
00208| ```
00209| 
00210| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00211| export async function getUserById(id) {
00212|   const data = await fetch(`https://...`, {
00213|     next: { tags: ['user'] },
00214|   })
00215| }
00216| ```
00217| 
00218| For non-`fetch` functions, `unstable_cache` also accepts a `tags` option (see [example above](#unstable_cache-for-non-fetch-functions)).
00219| 
00220| ### `revalidateTag`
00221| 
00222| Invalidate cached data by tag using [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag):
00223| 
00224| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
00225| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00226| 
00227| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00228|   // Mutate data
00229|   revalidateTag('user', 'max')
00230| }
00231| ```
00232| 
00233| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
00234| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00235| 
00236| export async function updateUser(id) {
00237|   // Mutate data
00238|   revalidateTag('user', 'max')
00239| }
00240| ```
00241| 
00242| ### `revalidatePath`
00243| 
00244| Invalidate all cached data for a specific route path using [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath):
00245| 
00246| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" switcher
00247| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00248| 
00249| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00250|   // Mutate data
00251|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00252| }
00253| ```
00254| 
00255| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" switcher
00256| import { revalidatePath } from 'next/cache'
00257| 
00258| export async function updateUser(id) {
00259|   // Mutate data
00260|   revalidatePath('/profile')
00261| }
00262| ```
00263| 
00264| ## Deduplicating requests
00265| 
00266| If you are not using `fetch` (which is [automatically memoized](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/fetch#memoization)), and instead using an ORM or database directly, you can wrap your data access with the [React `cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) function to deduplicate requests within a single render pass:
00267| 
00268| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00269| import { cache } from 'react'
00270| import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
00271| 
00272| export const getPost = cache(async (id: string) => {
00273|   const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
00274|     where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
00275|   })
00276| })
00277| ```
00278| 
00279| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00280| import { cache } from 'react'
00281| import { db, posts, eq } from '@/lib/db'
00282| 
00283| export const getPost = cache(async (id) => {
00284|   const post = await db.query.posts.findFirst({
00285|     where: eq(posts.id, parseInt(id)),
00286|   })
00287| })
00288| ```
00289| 
00290| ## Preloading data
00291| 
00292| You can preload data by creating a utility function that you eagerly call above blocking requests. This lets you initiate data fetching early, so the data is already available by the time the component renders.
00293| 
00294| Combine the [`server-only` package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/server-only) with React's [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to create a reusable preload utility:
00295| 
00296| ```ts filename="utils/get-item.ts" switcher
00297| import { cache } from 'react'
00298| import 'server-only'
00299| 
00300| export const getItem = cache(async (id: string) => {
00301|   // ...
00302| })
00303| 
00304| export const preload = (id: string) => {
00305|   void getItem(id)
00306| }
00307| ```
00308| 
00309| ```js filename="utils/get-item.js" switcher
00310| import { cache } from 'react'
00311| import 'server-only'
00312| 
00313| export const getItem = cache(async (id) => {
00314|   // ...
00315| })
00316| 
00317| export const preload = (id) => {
00318|   void getItem(id)
00319| }
00320| ```
00321| 
00322| Then call `preload()` before any blocking work so the data starts loading immediately:
00323| 
00324| ```tsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
00325| import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
00326| 
00327| export default async function Page({
00328|   params,
00329| }: {
00330|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00331| }) {
00332|   const { id } = await params
00333|   // Start loading item data
00334|   preload(id)
00335|   // Perform another asynchronous task
00336|   const isAvailable = await checkIsAvailable()

00338|   return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
00339| }
00340| 
00341| async function Item({ id }: { id: string }) {
00342|   const result = await getItem(id)
00343|   // ...
00344| }
00345| ```
00346| 
00347| ```jsx filename="app/item/[id]/page.js" switcher
00348| import { getItem, preload, checkIsAvailable } from '@/lib/data'
00349| 
00350| export default async function Page({ params }) {

00354|   // Perform another asynchronous task

00356| 
00357|   return isAvailable ? <Item id={id} /> : null
00358| }
00359| 
00360| async function Item({ id }) {
00361|   const result = await getItem(id)
00362|   // ...
00363| }
00364| ```

00367|
